text:
maria_s: Quick heads-up — I ran a stress pass on the continuous batcher with the new queue-budget target (tokens_per_batch=4096) and started seeing KV-cache OOM spikes when we mix long-context assistant traces with short chat queries.

aj: Can you paste the repro settings? Was this on the sparse or dense path? :thinking_face:

maria_s: Dense path on A100s. Workload: 30% long (8k tok), 70% short (<=128). Batcher config: 
```
batcher:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  max_requests: 64
  kv_budget_ratio: 0.6
  queue_policy: oldest_first
  allow_partial_on_timeout: true
```

leo: kv_budget_ratio 0.6 seems aggressive when long traces allocate big KV segments. What were the memory stats?

maria_s: From the run: 
- host mem free before: 320GB
- peak kv pages: 280GB
- gpu mem warnings: intermittent
- oom events (container): 3 over 10k requests

neha: Interesting. Did the batcher trim by tokens or by estimated kv bytes? We currently estimate KV size = seq_len * head_kv_scale (approx).

maria_s: We only trim by tokens. No estimation of kv bytes in admission. That's probably the problem.

aj: Proposed quick fix: include an admission check that computes estimated_kv_bytes for the batch and rejects (or trims) beyond per-GPU kv_threshold. Pseudocode: 
```
estimated_kv = sum(req.seq_len) * kv_per_token
if current_kv + estimated_kv > kv_threshold:
  if allow_partial: trim_smallest_requests()
  else reject_new_requests()
```

leo: +1. Also, change queue_policy to favor larger requests for long-tail workloads? We should avoid packing a single 8k with many 128s if it pushes kv above threshold. Maybe a hybrid: prefer oldest but if oldest pushes kv over threshold, try next that fits.

neha: We should add a soft budget target instead of hard reject: allow burst to 1.1*kv_threshold for <200ms to avoid latency regressions, then aggressively drain cache. That buys throughput while preventing sudden OOMs.

maria_s: Good call. I sketched a flow: 1) admission estimates kv_bytes; 2) if over soft_threshold, try re-ordering (next-fit) for a short window; 3) if still over hard_threshold, trim or reject. Also emit metric kv_batch_admission_rejections.

aj: Can we derive kv_per_token from model metadata instead of heuristics? Training artifacts store cached_kv_size_per_token for model shards. Use that to make estimates accurate across quantized variants.

maria_s: Yep, I'll plumb that in. One wrinkle: for quantized kernels we see slightly smaller KV footprint — store variant overrides in the model profile.

leo: For rollout, want a canary with these changes and telemetry: kv_estimate_error, admission_reorders, rejections, avg_batch_kv_bytes, and tail latency. Keep default behavior unchanged unless canary passes.

neha: Also add a debug flag to log sample batches that triggered re-ordering so we can inspect failure modes. Could be useful to tune next-fit vs best-fit heuristics.

infra-bot: deploy requested: batcher-kv-admission v1 -> canary cluster [canary-3]. CI checks: unit tests: pass. perf-run: scheduled.

maria_s: I'll run a focused perf sweep (mix ratios 10/90, 30/70, 50/50) and post results. Expect to iterate on kv_budget_ratio default.

aj: Thanks — if you hit OOMs again, ping me with the sample logs. I can instrument per-page allocations to see fragmentation. :mag_right:

maria_s: Will do. Putting a short RFC in eng-runtime channel tomorrow with the heuristic design and metrics.

leo: Nice work. If this reduces OOMs without hurting p99, big win for Dedicated customers. :rocket:
